source.excerpt: RFC: migrate session storage from Redis to Postgres

scqa.situation: Sessions live in a dedicated Redis cluster.
scqa.complication: The cluster caused two incidents and costs more than the database it fronts.
scqa.question: Should we move sessions into Postgres?
scqa.answer: Move session storage to Postgres in Q1, behind a dual-write flag.

keyLine.claim: Redis is now the riskiest part of the login path.

children.claim: Two of the last three login incidents started in Redis.
Failover dropped every session in the March incident.
support: Postmortem PM-212: 41 minutes of forced logouts.

children.claim: Memory eviction logged users out during the June peak.
The maxmemory policy evicts live sessions first.
support: allkeys-lru was set in 2021 and never revisited.

children.claim: Nobody on the team owns Redis operations.
support: The last Redis owner left in 2024; the runbook is stale.

keyLine.claim: Postgres can carry session load with headroom.

children.claim: Peak session reads fit the current primary.
support: Load test: 9k reads/s at p99 4 ms on the existing instance.

children.claim: Writes stay small because sessions change rarely.
support: Only 3% of requests mutate a session.

keyLine.claim: So moving sessions to Postgres removes the risk at lower cost.

children.claim: One fewer datastore saves about $14k a year.
support: Current Redis cluster invoice, averaged over 12 months.

children.claim: A dual-write flag makes rollback a config change.
support: The flag pattern is already used for the billing migration.

notes: The RFC does not estimate migration engineering effort.
governingThought: Move session storage to Postgres in Q1, behind a dual-write flag.
